chunks: Muhammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muhammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān, from Abū Nuʿaym, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Aʿyān, who said:

We performed al-Ṭamattuʿ (combining ʿUmrah and Ḥajj) and entered into iḥrām, and with us were young boys who entered into iḥrām and responded to the call (talbiyah) just as we did. We could not afford to sacrifice sheep. He said, 'Let the guardian of each boy fast.' And whoever had clothes with which he adorned and beautified himself, and had no other clothes, he is not required to sell them for the price of the sacrifice; rather, fasting suffices for him. Narrated.

key_terms.أَحْرَمْنَا: We entered into the state of Ihram
key_terms.تَمَتَّعْنَا: We performed al-Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the alternative expiation for those who cannot afford the sacrificial animal during al-Tamattu' Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the *ḥady* of *Ṭamattuʿ*, emphasizing that fasting is a valid substitute when financial means are lacking, even for children who perform Hajj with their guardians. It further clarifies the principle of ease (*taysīr*) by exempting those whose only garments are their *iḥrām* clothes from the obligation to sell them, thereby preventing undue hardship. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on practicality and the removal of burden in ritual obligations.
